questions.stem: Which AWS framework helps organizations plan their cloud adoption, organizing guidance into perspectives such as Business, People and Governance?

options.rationale: Well-Architected reviews workload design against six pillars, not adoption perspectives.
AWS CAF groups its capabilities into six perspectives: Business, People, Governance, Platform, Security and Operations.
The shared responsibility model divides security duties between AWS and the customer.
Trusted Advisor checks your account against best practices.

questions.explanation: AWS CAF uses AWS experience and best practices to help organizations digitally transform and accelerate business outcomes through the cloud.

questions.stem: Which is a business outcome that AWS CAF identifies as a benefit of cloud transformation?

options.rationale: Cloud adoption generally reduces up-front capital spending.
Cloud adoption aims to speed up delivery, not slow it.
AWS CAF lists reduced business risk, improved ESG performance, increased revenue and increased operational efficiency.
Moving to the cloud reduces the hardware you manage.

questions.explanation: AWS CAF describes four business outcomes: reduced business risk, improved environmental, social and governance (ESG) performance, increased revenue and increased operational efficiency.

questions.stem: Which AWS CAF perspective focuses on culture, organizational structure, leadership and workforce skills?

options.rationale: Platform focuses on building the enterprise-grade cloud platform.
Security focuses on confidentiality, integrity and availability of data and workloads.
Operations focuses on delivering cloud services at the level the business needs.
The People perspective bridges technology and business, helping evolve culture and skills.

questions.explanation: The six AWS CAF perspectives are Business, People, Governance, Platform, Security and Operations.

questions.stem: Which AWS CAF perspective helps make sure cloud services are delivered at a level that meets the needs of the business, covering areas such as monitoring and incident management?

options.rationale: The Operations perspective covers observability, event and incident management, and other operational capabilities.
Governance focuses on orchestrating initiatives, managing risk and controlling spending.
People focuses on culture and skills.
Business focuses on making sure cloud investments accelerate business outcomes.

questions.explanation: The Operations perspective helps ensure cloud services are delivered at a level that meets the needs of the business.

questions.stem: A company moves an application from its data center to Amazon EC2 without changing the application's code. Which migration strategy is this?

options.rationale: Refactoring changes the application's architecture to use cloud-native features.
Rehosting, also called lift and shift, moves an application to the cloud without changes.
Repurchasing replaces the application with a different product, often SaaS.
Retiring decommissions an application that is no longer needed.

questions.explanation: The migration strategies are often called the 7 Rs: retire, retain, rehost, relocate, repurchase, replatform and refactor.

questions.stem: A company replaces its self-managed customer relationship management software with a software as a service (SaaS) product during its migration. Which migration strategy is this?

options.rationale: Rehosting moves the same application without changes.
Relocating moves infrastructure, such as VMware workloads, to the cloud without new hardware or application changes.
Repurchasing, also called drop and shop, moves to a different product, typically SaaS.
Retaining keeps the application where it is for now.

questions.explanation: Repurchase replaces an existing application with a different one, often a SaaS offering.

questions.stem: During migration, a company moves its self-managed database to Amazon RDS but leaves the application's core architecture unchanged. Which migration strategy is this?

options.rationale: Rehosting makes no changes at all.
Refactoring re-architects the application.
Retiring switches the application off.
Replatforming makes a few cloud optimizations, such as moving to a managed database, without changing the core architecture.

questions.explanation: Replatform, sometimes called lift, tinker and shift, gains some cloud benefits without re-architecting.

questions.stem: Which migration strategy involves re-architecting an application to use cloud-native features, for example rebuilding it with serverless services?

options.rationale: Refactoring (re-architecting) changes how the application is built to take full advantage of cloud-native features.
Rehosting moves the application as is.
Retaining keeps the application in its current environment.
Repurchasing replaces the application with another product.

questions.explanation: Refactoring is usually driven by a strong business need for scale, performance or new features that the current architecture cannot provide.

questions.stem: A company wants to migrate an on-premises database to AWS while the source database stays fully operational during the migration. Which service should it use?

options.rationale: DataSync transfers files and objects, not live database migrations.
AWS DMS migrates databases to AWS while the source remains operational, minimizing downtime.
AWS Backup centralizes backups; it is not a migration tool.
Athena queries data in Amazon S3.

questions.explanation: AWS DMS supports homogeneous and heterogeneous migrations and can keep replicating changes until you cut over.

questions.stem: Which TWO are migration strategies among the AWS 7 Rs? (Choose TWO.)

options.rationale: Rebooting is not a migration strategy.
Relocate moves infrastructure to the cloud without buying new hardware or changing applications.
Reselling is not a migration strategy.
Retain keeps an application in its current environment for now.
Rebuilding hardware is not one of the migration strategies.

questions.explanation: The 7 Rs are retire, retain, rehost, relocate, repurchase, replatform and refactor.

questions.stem: Which service automates lift-and-shift (rehost) migrations of physical, virtual or cloud servers to AWS?

options.rationale: AWS DMS migrates databases, not whole servers.

options.text: AWS Application Migration Service (now AWS Transform MGN)
options.rationale: Application Migration Service replicates source servers and launches them on AWS with minimal changes.
AWS SCT converts database schemas.
AWS Config records resource configurations.

questions.explanation: AWS Application Migration Service, now called AWS Transform MGN, is the recommended service for rehosting physical, virtual and cloud servers on AWS.

questions.stem: Which service collects information about on-premises servers, their configuration and their usage to help plan a migration?

options.rationale: CloudTrail records API activity in AWS accounts.
Inspector scans AWS workloads for vulnerabilities.
Application Discovery Service gathers data about on-premises servers and their dependencies.
AWS Config records AWS resource configurations, not on-premises servers.

questions.explanation: Discovery data helps you size targets and decide which migration strategy fits each application. AWS Application Discovery Service is no longer open to new customers (AWS points to AWS Transform instead), but the CLF-C02 exam guide still lists it.

questions.stem: A company wants partners to keep uploading files with SFTP, but store the files in Amazon S3. Which service supports this?

options.rationale: CloudFront delivers content to users.
Direct Connect is a private network connection.
Route 53 is a DNS service.
Transfer Family provides managed SFTP, FTPS and FTP endpoints backed by Amazon S3 or Amazon EFS.

questions.explanation: Transfer Family is part of the migration and transfer category in the exam guide.

questions.stem: During migration planning, a company finds an application that nobody uses any more. Which migration strategy applies?

options.rationale: Retiring decommissions applications that are no longer needed, which reduces cost and risk.
Rehosting moves the application as is.
Replatforming moves it with some optimizations.
Refactoring re-architects it.

questions.explanation: Discovery often finds applications that can simply be switched off instead of migrated.

questions.stem: Which AWS CAF perspective focuses on building an enterprise-grade, scalable cloud platform and modernizing existing workloads?

options.rationale: People covers culture and skills.
The Platform perspective covers platform architecture, engineering and modernization.
Governance covers risk, portfolio and cost management.
Business covers aligning cloud investments with business outcomes.

questions.explanation: Business, People and Governance are business-focused perspectives; Platform, Security and Operations are technical.
